title: Submit a valid parent whose pre_root/h_pre is not the current anchored state
verdictRule: Settle cases (evaluator rule fixed 2026-10-25 before any settle submission). REJECT = either (a) the node refuses the attempt at submission with an RPC 1010 Invalid Transaction refusal and its hash is absent from the indexer, or (b) it is included with an indexed result other than SUCCESS and the target's latest contract action is unchanged by it. Not counted, in either form: refusals or failures about fees, DUST or balance, the pool's 1012 temporary ban, or TTL expiry. Both forms also need the native proof-verifying ledger-9 predictor to apply the same proven call over the snapshot it claims and refuse it on the target, so the refusal is caused by the ledger state the transcript reads. And both need the control settle C, from the same harness and run, to have finalized with SUCCESS and an indexed post-state equal to the harness VM prediction. A refusal in the prover (SettleUnsatisfiable) is local and never counts.

target.evidenceProducer: qa/holdout/lib/stagenet/produce-a9-settle.mjs (proofs only under heavy.lock; one fresh wallet session per transaction; WALLET BUSY/FREE and ACQUIRE/RELEASE on #sherlock)
target.contractNote: D2: fresh owner-authorized deployment of the same source, keys and constructor as ac93b80e (instance_id identical); acceptValidity(A8 stmt) tx 5f3ae140...85e5 block 1016423; S0 = indexed post-state e4bb4589...

mutation.description: settleValidity proven against a snapshot whose (root, height) is not the chain's current anchored head

expectedTargetBehavior: ledger refuses both stale and forged-head settles; no state change; control settle finalizes

seed.note: Stagenet definitions by the evaluator, 2026-10-24, from the contract source and the A8 adapter; see definition/rationale.

requirementRefs: ZR10 stale head, UISEC-011, link anchor (pre_root, h_pre)
definition: Two ledger-observable forms, both needed. (1) Stale head (ZR10): P1 = prepareSettle(S0, 0, A3 fields) is prepared from the live pre-settle snapshot S0 but submitted only after the control settle C (same inputs, prepared separately) has finalized; the chain's (R, H, B) is now (post_root, H0+2, 1). (2) Forged head: P2 = prepareSettle(S0', 0, fields'), where S0' sets root := R' != R, fields'[6] = R', fields'[15] = settleTrace(S0', fields') and validity_ok contains settleStatement(S0', 0, fields'). P2 is submitted while the chain root is still R. Each must be refused by the ledger, not indexed, with the indexed state unchanged.
rationale: Every settleValidity guard (predecessor root, h_pre, h_post, trace order) is an in-circuit assertion over values the transcript reads from the ledger. A mutated fields vector against the true state is unsatisfiable, so it fails in the prover, which is a local refusal and does not count. The guard is observable at the ledger only as a transcript whose ledger reads (root, height, batch_no, set membership) differ from chain state at execution, which is exactly a wrong or stale predecessor. Positive control: settle C must finalize with indexed settled containing stmt, root = f9, height = H0+2 and batch_no = 1.
positiveControl: Control settle C = prepareSettle(S0, 0, A3 fields) submitted first; it must finalize with the indexed post-state equal to report.predictedPostStateSHA256.

exports.settleTrace(snapshot, fields): -> bigint: f15 as the contract computes it (TRACE_ORDER over the snapshot's pins and (R, H))
exports.settleStatement(snapshot, batch, fields): -> bigint: stmt as settleValidity computes it (SHK_STMT, I, current B, ...)

requirements: snapshot is a ledger-9 ContractState for the pinned address. The settleValidity circuit is executed and proven against exactly this snapshot: the evaluator passes either the live indexed state (recorded height) or a copy whose data it edited (root, height, batch_no, validity_ok, settled). The harness must not re-fetch chain state, compare the snapshot to the chain, or refuse because they differ.
batch is a bigint; fields are 16 bigints in W-instance order f0..f15.

The proof comes from the proof server with the installed compiled settleValidity key (verifier SHA-256 be8b0943...0b5c, as installed on the pin). The only client-side refusal allowed is the circuit itself being unsatisfiable over the snapshot; then throw an Error named SettleUnsatisfiable before any wallet use.

tx is the wallet-balanced, finalized ledger Transaction, held in memory and never written to disk or logged; TTL >= 30 minutes so a prepared tx can be held while another is submitted. The harness never submits; the evaluator submits with session.walletProvider.submitTx.
report = {snapshotSHA256, predictedPostStateSHA256 (VM over the snapshot), stmt}. The wallet comes only from tools/sherlock-sdk/stagenet-session.mjs; no seed, key or transaction body is logged.
